leads.claim: 'cosmic_correct' route: Cosmic Duality blob 'decrypted' (cosmic_decrypted.bin) -> 39 x 32-byte blocks -> address payload block[16:32]||BE32(X) -> 39 Base58Check P2PKH addresses (file name says 12: '7x1H + 5x1B = 12 unique', issue #91)
leads.method: AES (openssl) decrypt of the Cosmic blob with an unstated password, then fixed block slicing
leads.self_verifying: NOT self-verifying as given: Base58Check checksums are computed by the solver, so every 20-byte payload yields a 'valid' address. Real test = re-decrypt the 1328-byte Cosmic ciphertext with the claimed password and check padding beyond 1 byte + plaintext structure/entropy; a random 0x01 pad hits 1/256. Optional: any on-chain history on these addresses would be informative.

leads.claim: A 79-byte 'plaintext' from the SalPhaseIon-size blob (80-byte ciphertext) i.e. 1-byte PKCS#7 pad
leads.self_verifying: Head bytes are high-entropy, not text: classic 1/256 single-byte-padding false positive unless the password is shown and the bytes have structure

leads.claim: dbbi (91 = C(14,2)) as upper triangle of a symmetric 14x14 matrix; row sums = 14-value key; faed rows of 15 summed (38 values); chr((R xor K) mod 26 + 65)
leads.self_verifying: Ran it: S contains 'SENDTHE' at pos 11-17 but the rest is gibberish; ad-hoc decoder with many free choices (xor vs add, mod 26, widths 14/15, zeroing variants) -> look-elsewhere; not self-verifying. dbbi-as-triangle idea already explored in research/evidence/cycle02/_work__matrixtri.py
